sources.kelvinHalfAngleDeg/cuspWaveAngleDeg: Deep-water Kelvin wake: half-angle arcsin(1/3) = 19.47 deg, waves on the cusp line travel at arctan(1/sqrt(2)) = 35.26 deg to the track. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelvin_wake_pattern
sources.wavenumbers: Stationary pattern in the boat frame with deep-water dispersion omega^2 = g k (waves.json sources): transverse k = g / V^2 (wavelength 2 pi V^2 / g), cusp waves k = g / (V cos 35.26 deg)^2.
sources.sourceAmplitude: Energy balance: wave-making resistance = energy left behind per metre of track = 1/2 rho g A^2 * width (linear wave energy density, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airy_wave_theory). R_w is the Delft residuary resistance (docs/bare_hull_resistance.pdf p6, sim hull layer) at the boat's speed; it also contains some viscous-pressure drag, so the amplitude is an upper estimate. effectiveWidthFracBeam (width = 1.0 x beam) is TUNING GUESS.
sources.divergentDecayExponent/transverseDecayEx: TUNING GUESS: amplitude decay with distance behind the bow as s^-1/3 along the cusp lines and s^-1/2 for transverse waves, the usual stationary-phase scalings [INFERENCE]; not from a file in docs/.
sources.transverseFrac/armWidthFracWavelength/ar: TUNING GUESS: visual envelope of the arms and the inner transverse waves, and an age e-folding time standing in for viscous decay and spreading.
sources.visualGain: TUNING GUESS, render only: multiplies the Kelvin source amplitude (1 = the energy-balance upper estimate). Reduced from 1.5 to 0.4 after the isolated boat-wake screenshot showed oversized ridges (about 73% lower height), then raised to 0.8 at the user's request because the Kelvin waves read as small next to the bow waves; wavelengths and shader work unchanged. This is a visual choice, not measured Laser wake data.
sources.bowHeadFrac: TUNING GUESS, render only: bow wave height as a fraction of stagnation head V^2 / (2 g) (Bernoulli). Increased from 0.06 to 0.16, then to 0.30 at the user's request for a more prominent bow V: 1.875 times the 0.16 height, about 6.1 cm at 2 m/s. Kelvin gain, packet propagation, source history and sim forces are unchanged. This is visual tuning, not measured Laser wake data.
sources.bowLength/bowOffset/bowWidth/bowAngleDeg: TUNING GUESS, render only: emitted circular crest/trough packets, with radial profile (1 - 2 u^2) exp(-u^2). Each packet retains its birth contact, height and speed; radius = bowOffset + c * age, width = bowWidth + bowWidthGrowth * radius, amplitude attenuates as 1 / sqrt(1 + radius / bowLength), bowLength raised from 3 to 5 m so the V arms persist farther out. c = birth surge * sin(bowAngleDeg) makes the envelope of successive expanding circles a 30-degree V in steady straight motion (a nondispersive geometric approximation, not measured Laser wave propagation). Emission period = 2 pi c / g, from deep-water omega^2 = g k and c = omega/k; packets themselves are not a full dispersive or fluid solver.
sources.bowDecayTime/bowMaxAge/bowFronts/bowFiel: TUNING GUESS: render-only emitted-wave lifetime and resolution. Age e-folding 7 s; expiry 12 s with fade over the last birth period; smooth birth over 0.25 of a period. Up to 128 fronts, covering 12 s at the minimum emitting speed. A 256-square field covers 64 m around the boat on a logical-world grid; cache edges fade over four cells. Overlap normalization uses both envelope and absolute signed-profile mass, bounding positive crests AND dense overlapping troughs within the source-height scale without clipping height. The float texture is sampled with manual bilinear interpolation, so float-linear texture support is not required. These are visual/numerical choices, not measured wake data.
sources.contactSamples: Render-only longitudinal contact-search resolution: 64 bow-to-transom intervals; transverse samples reuse laser.json visual.sectionPoints. The cached loft is transformed in the same heel/pitch/yaw order as the boat mesh. Hull/sea crossings are refined along sampled edges. Only new wave/foam contributions originate at the foremost wet contact; already-emitted fronts retain their birth positions. No clearance fade.
sources.trailSpacing/trailPoints/maxAge/teleport: Render resolution and bookkeeping: 40 points x 0.75 m = 30 m of world-anchored trail; a jump above teleportDistance or time going back (reset) clears it.
sources.foam*: VISUAL ESTIMATE: turbulent wake foam behind the transom (width, spread, fade, speed threshold), whitewater on the bow-wave crest, world-anchored periodic noise (period 64 m, slow drift rates in rad/s).
sources.foamBowThreshold/foamBowFull/foamBowGain: TUNING GUESS, render only: crest coverage starts at 0.18 and reaches full at 0.65 of the emitted source height, with gain 1.4. Bow foam uses the same noise patch breakup as stern foam (smoothstep over 0.3 of the noise range, threshold set by coverage), so grain and patch scale match; coverage varies continuously so crest foam thins smoothly instead of switching off. Birth speed coverage starts at the bow emission minSpeed and uses foamSpeedRange, independently of stern foam's foamMinSpeed. Stored birth coverage and packet aging preserve foam history on dry/stop transitions. Stern foam appearance is unchanged.
